verdict.left_looks: A dark-brown timber pavilion on a stone-brick plinth. Stepped, pyramidal roof in dark wood-plank stair-steps with wide overhanging eaves. Open colonnade of tall dark pillars with a few small window gaps, a raised wooden deck with rail, and lantern torches at the corners. Entrance is a stone step cut into the front deck. Very uniform single-material palette; reads as an open pavilion or gazebo more than an enclosed house, and the roof looks like a stacked lid over an open frame.
verdict.right_looks: An enclosed timber house with a dark grey stepped-tile roof, curved-looking eave tips and small ridge detail (chimney block, stone-slab trim). Dark log-style walls with pale window panes, a wooden lower band, and a mossy stone-and-grass plinth with dirt base, a stone stair at the front, and a lantern on a post. Mixed materials (stone, moss, grass, dirt) read as deliberate weathered style rather than damage. Asymmetric side extension and a chimney add character; the roof reads as a proper Japanese-style house roof.
verdict.why: The right build has a fuller enclosed massing with walls, a layered roof with eave detail and chimney, and a planted, grounded plinth that give it clear character, while the left reads as an open single-material pavilion with a flat-looking roof lid over a bare frame.
